text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Laurent Kabila, is due to arrive in Windhoek later today for a two-day official visit, with Namibia's plans to tap water from the Congo River expected to feature on the agenda.

- Work ground to a halt at Meatco's abattoir in Windhoek on Friday when close to 400 workers went on strike to press their demand for a decent wage and for the sacking of the entire board of the government-owned company. Namibia Wholesale and Retail Workers' Union (NWRWU) Secretary general Aloysius Yon accused Meatco's management of negotiating in bad faith after an earlier wage agreement collapsed.

- The president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Laurent Kabila arrives for a two-day official visit to Namibia today. At midday the guest will be honoured with a Windhoek street being given his name.
- Three people were shot dead by a man in Windhoek on Friday, before he turned the AK 47 on himself.

- The Namibia Wholesale and Retail Workers' Union and its secretary general, Aloysius Yon, face criminal charges after three employees of Meatco, among them a woman, were seriously assaulted by striking workers on Friday.
- Five toddlers and a baby were the victims of rape and sodomy over the weekend.

- Members of the former South West Africa Territory Force (SWATF) are planning to stage a demonstration this Friday to demand the N$ 36 million given to them by the South African government, which they say was not paid out to them in full by the Namibian government.

- In the latest twist of events in the Divundu controversy, the ministry of regional, local government and housing has revealed that neither of the two chiefs vying for the upper hand is recognised by the government. The controversy involves Mbukushu headman Erwin Mbambo and Kxoe chief Kippie George and began with government's announcement to extend a penal centre in an area claimed by both George and Mbambo as traditional land.

- Mike Moles, Exploration manager for southern Africa, Reunion Mining (Zimbabwe) Limited, is of the opinion that the Skorpion Mine situated in the Sperrgebiet could turn out to be the largest Zinc mine in the world. A joint venture between Reunion and Anglo American Mining, the mine is currently in the midst of drilling to determine the feasibility of the project.
